summary: Materials innovation money is mostly government money aimed at breaking China's hold on rare earths, magnets, gallium and graphite, with price floors, equity stakes and loans doing the work that markets will not. Two November 2026 deadlines on China's export controls are the swing factor. Battery and chip materials are the commercial frontier: sodium ion is reaching scale in China, while SiC has turned into a commodity and GaN and glass substrates ride the AI data center power shift.

innovations.name: Rare earth magnets and recycling
innovations.what: Making neodymium iron boron magnets outside China, and recovering rare earths from old motors, hard drives and scrap. These magnets sit in every EV motor, wind turbine, drone, missile and robot.
innovations.stage_why: US magnet plants have started shipping: USA Rare Earth began filling orders in Q2 2026 and MP Materials sent magnets to GM for qualification, with commercial shipments due Q4 2026. Volumes are still tiny next to China, and recycling is just reaching its first commercial plants.

evidence.cost: NdPr oxide sold in the high $90s/kg in Q3 2026 (MP guidance), below the $110/kg floor the Pentagon guarantees to MP; the government pays the gap.
evidence.approvals: July 2025 DoD deal gives MP a 10 year $110/kg NdPr price floor and 100% offtake of its 10X magnet plant. USA Rare Earth expected a $1.6 billion Commerce Department CHIPS funding agreement in May 2026 (signing unverified this session).
evidence.money: DoD took about a 15% stake in MP for $400 million (2025). USA Rare Earth closed a $1.5 billion private stock sale in January 2026. Vulcan Elements and ReElement got a $1.4 billion package including a $620 million DoD loan. Recycler Cyclic Materials raised $75 million in August 2026, $237 million total.
evidence.revenue: MP Q2 2026 revenue was $108.5 million plus $17.6 million of price floor income; its magnet segment earned $16.5 million. USA Rare Earth Stillwater Phase 1a targets 600 tonnes per year by end of 2026 and 1,200 tonnes in Q1 2027.

spreads_to.use: EV and hybrid traction motors
Missiles, drones, jet actuators; US rules bar Chinese magnets in weapons from 2027 (unverified this session)
Humanoid and industrial robot joints each use many small magnets
Phones, hard drives, speakers, a key source of recyclable scrap

innovations.bottleneck: Heavy rare earths (dysprosium and terbium) for heat resistant magnets. China controls nearly all separation; outside China only Lynas and, from late 2027, Energy Fuels make meaningful amounts. China's one year suspension of its October 2025 export rules ends November 10, 2026.

next_milestone.event: China decision on the rare earth export rule suspension; MP first commercial magnet shipments to GM

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if China extends the suspension and floods the market with cheap magnets while US buyers refuse to pay a premium beyond defense volumes.

innovations.name: Critical mineral processing outside China
innovations.what: Refining and processing the metals that China dominates, such as gallium, germanium, antimony, graphite anode and lithium chemicals, in the US and allied countries.
innovations.stage_why: First Western plants are producing (Syrah's Louisiana graphite anode plant) or under construction with government money (Alcoa gallium, Korea Zinc Tennessee), but output is a small fraction of Chinese supply.

evidence.cost: China and Chinese controlled firms are forecast to hold about 99.1% of global battery anode capacity in 2026. Battery grade lithium carbonate was about $24,000 to $25,000/t in May 2026, up about 60% that year, then turned down.
evidence.approvals: China's suspension of its gallium, germanium and antimony export ban to the US ends November 27, 2026; the military end user ban stays. US price floors, equity stakes and Project Vault stockpile buying act as de facto approvals for chosen producers.
evidence.money: Project Vault stockpile: $10 billion EXIM loan plus $1.67 billion private (February 2026). Alcoa reached final investment decision on a 100 t/yr gallium plant in July 2026 with $174 million of Pentagon support. Korea Zinc plans a $7.4 billion Tennessee smelter with the US holding 40% of the venture. DOE took 5% of Lithium Americas.
evidence.revenue: Syrah began producing active anode material at its 11,250 t/yr Vidalia, Louisiana plant, with Tesla to take 8,000 t/yr once qualified. Novonix is building toward 20,000 t/yr of synthetic graphite in Chattanooga with Panasonic and PowerCo offtakes.

spreads_to.use: Gallium and germanium for chips, lasers and GaN power devices
Antimony for ammunition, tungsten for armor piercing rounds
Graphite anode and lithium chemicals for batteries
Germanium for fiber optics, gallium for power chips

innovations.bottleneck: Processing know how and permits, not ore. China holds most refining capacity and the process engineers. Outside China a few firms (Alcoa, Umicore, Korea Zinc, Syrah) and government money decide what gets built.

next_milestone.event: China decision on the gallium, germanium and antimony ban suspension

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if China extends suspensions and dumps material to undercut Western plants, and US policy support (floors, stockpiles) is cut after the 2026 midterms.

innovations.name: Next generation batteries: solid state and sodium ion
innovations.what: Solid state cells swap liquid electrolyte for a solid one to store more energy and charge faster. Sodium ion cells use cheap, plentiful sodium instead of lithium, mainly for grid storage and low cost EVs.
innovations.stage_why: Sodium ion is moving to early adoption in China, with CATL starting large scale output in Q4 2026. Solid state is still at pilot lines and car maker sample testing, with no mass market car on sale.

evidence.cost: CATL sodium ion cells are quoted at about $50 to $56/kWh in 2026 (industry estimates, unverified) against Chinese LFP storage cells at about CNY 0.365/Wh in April 2026, so sodium is near cost parity. Solid state has no public cost figure; it costs more than lithium ion today.
evidence.approvals: Automotive qualification is the gate: QuantumScape is shipping Cobra based B1 samples and Solid Power is in a joint evaluation with Samsung SDI and BMW.
evidence.money: QuantumScape opened its Eagle pilot line on February 4, 2026 with PowerCo (Volkswagen) as lead partner and Murata and Corning as ceramics partners. Peak Energy plans a 4 GWh sodium ion storage factory in California (July 2026). Sodium ion shipments are forecast at 20 to 27 GWh in 2026 and over 400 GWh by 2030 (industry forecasts).
evidence.revenue: Solid Power had only $2.8 million of revenue and grants in H1 2026. QuantumScape has licensing and development payments but no product sales. CATL expects sodium ion cells in up to 20,000 EVs by end of 2026.

spreads_to.use: Sodium ion for cheap, safe stationary batteries
High energy solid state cells for eVTOL and drones
Thinner, safer phone and wearable batteries
Batteries without lithium or Chinese graphite

innovations.bottleneck: For solid state: sulfide electrolyte and ceramic separator manufacturing at scale, held by a few firms (Solid Power, Murata, Idemitsu). For sodium ion: hard carbon anode supply, mostly Chinese. CATL and BYD control the factories that can scale sodium fastest.

next_milestone.event: CATL sodium ion large scale output; Solid Power continuous electrolyte line commissioning

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if lithium prices keep falling so LFP stays cheaper than sodium, or if solid state samples fail car maker validation and launch dates slip past 2029.

innovations.name: New chip materials: GaN, SiC and glass substrates
innovations.what: Gallium nitride (GaN) and silicon carbide (SiC) chips switch power with less waste than silicon, for EVs, chargers and AI server racks. Glass core substrates replace organic packaging so very large AI chips stay flat and pack more wiring.
innovations.stage_why: SiC is mass market in EVs, GaN is mass market in phone chargers, and both are now entering AI data centers through Nvidia's 800 V power design. Glass substrates are at pilot, with limited volume expected around 2028.

evidence.cost: SiC is commoditizing: Chinese 6 inch substrates are pushing prices down, and 6 inch epitaxial wafers are forecast to fall from about 7,300 yuan (2024) to 4,400 yuan by 2029. Wolfspeed's fiscal Q3 2026 revenue fell 18.9% to $150.2 million.
evidence.approvals: Nvidia named Navitas, Infineon and others as partners for its 800 V HVDC rack design (2025). SiC chips are qualified in most new EVs.
evidence.money: SKC put about KRW 590 billion of a KRW 1 trillion share sale into its glass substrate unit Absolics (2026), which finished the first dedicated glass substrate plant in Covington, Georgia in March 2026. Wolfspeed emerged from Chapter 11 on September 29, 2025 with debt cut about 70%. Intel teamed with Lens Technology on glass substrates in July 2026.
evidence.revenue: Navitas Q2 2026 revenue was only $10.5 million, so GaN for data centers is still small. Absolics samples are in reliability testing in Taiwan, with no volume sales yet.

spreads_to.use: 800 V DC power delivery and power supplies for megawatt racks
SiC inverters for longer EV range and faster charging
Solar inverters, battery storage and grid converters
GaN radar and electronic warfare

innovations.bottleneck: SiC is no longer scarce. The scarce inputs are qualified 200 mm GaN on silicon foundry capacity (TSMC is exiting GaN, unverified this session; GlobalFoundries, Infineon and Innoscience are scaling) and gallium itself, almost all refined in China. For glass, it is through glass via drilling and handling tools, held by LPKF, Corning and a few others.

next_milestone.event: Navitas first US made 200 mm GaN wafers from GlobalFoundries; Absolics reliability results

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if Nvidia's 800 V racks slip or use mostly silicon, or if Absolics and Intel push glass substrates past 2030.

innovations.name: Advanced composites
innovations.what: Carbon fiber and resin parts that are lighter and stronger than metal. New fast curing and thermoplastic types aim to make composite parts at car and drone speeds, not just a few jets a month.
innovations.stage_why: Carbon fiber is mature in wide body jets (787, A350), but higher rate thermoplastic parts, reusable rockets, eVTOL aircraft and hydrogen tanks are early. Demand is rising again as Airbus and Boeing lift build rates.

evidence.approvals: Aircraft certification by the FAA and EASA is the gate for new composite structures; eVTOL makers using carbon fiber airframes are still finishing type certification (status unverified this session).
evidence.money: Hexcel says it is restarting idle carbon fiber capacity and adding staff as build rates rise (Q2 2026). Rocket Lab's Neutron uses a carbon composite structure, showing launch makers' commitment.
evidence.revenue: Hexcel Q2 2026 sales were $529.3 million, up 8%, with commercial aerospace up 18.3%; 2026 guidance $2.025 to $2.125 billion. Hexcel sees about $500 million of extra annual sales if Airbus and Boeing reach target rates.

spreads_to.use: Carbon composite rocket stages and satellite structures
Drones, missiles and stealth airframes
Wind blades and hydrogen and gas pressure tanks
Lightweight battery enclosures and body parts in premium EVs

innovations.bottleneck: Aerospace grade carbon fiber and its feedstock acrylonitrile. Qualified supply sits with Toray (number one), Hexcel, Teijin and Syensqo, and new lines take years to qualify.

next_milestone.event: Airbus and Boeing rate increases (A350, 787) and Hexcel Q3 2026 results

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if Airbus or Boeing cut wide body rates again, which would leave carbon fiber capacity idle.
